# Feature Requirements: Slugify String Utility Function

## Overview

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility

**Description**: A reusable string utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs by applying a series of normalization and sanitization rules.

**Business Value**: Enables consistent generation of clean, readable URL slugs from user-provided or system-generated text, improving SEO, readability, and consistency across the application.

## Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Normalization to Lowercase
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**User Story**: As a developer, I want all input text converted to lowercase so that slugs are consistently formatted regardless of input casing.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN any input string with mixed case characters
- WHEN the slugify function is called
- THEN all alphabetic characters MUST be converted to lowercase
- Example: "Hello, World!" → contains "hello" and "world" in output

**Rationale**: Lowercase ensures consistency and follows common URL slug conventions used in web applications and SEO best practices.

---

### REQ-002: Space and Underscore Replacement
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**User Story**: As a developer, I want spaces and underscores replaced with hyphens so that slugs use standard URL-friendly separators.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN input text containing spaces (U+0020) or underscores (_)
- WHEN the slugify function is called
- THEN all spaces MUST be replaced with a single hyphen (-)
- AND all underscores MUST be replaced with a single hyphen (-)
- Example: "Foo Bar" → "foo-bar"
- Example: "Foo_Bar" → "foo-bar"

**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs, preferred over spaces (which encode as %20) and underscores for readability and SEO.

---

### REQ-003: Character Whitelist Enforcement
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**User Story**: As a developer, I want only safe characters retained so that the resulting slug is valid for use in URLs without encoding.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN input text containing any characters
- WHEN the slugify function is called
- THEN only the following characters MUST be retained:
  - Lowercase letters (a-z)
  - Numbers (0-9)
  - Hyphens (-)
- AND all other characters MUST be removed
- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
- Example: "Foo@Bar#123" → "foobar123" (@ and # removed)

**Rationale**: Restricting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures the slug is safe for URLs, file systems, and database identifiers without special encoding.

---

### REQ-004: Hyphen Consolidation
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**User Story**: As a developer, I want consecutive hyphens collapsed to a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN text that would produce multiple consecutive hyphens after character removal and replacement
- WHEN the slugify function is called
- THEN all sequences of 2 or more consecutive hyphens MUST be replaced with a single hyphen
- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
- Example: "Foo  Bar" → "foo-bar" (two spaces become one hyphen)
- Example: "Hello,,,World" → "helloworld" (commas removed, no extra hyphens)

**Rationale**: Multiple consecutive hyphens reduce readability and appear unprofessional in URLs.

---

### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**User Story**: As a developer, I want leading and trailing hyphens removed so that slugs start and end with meaningful content.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN text that would produce hyphens at the beginning or end after processing
- WHEN the slugify function is called
- THEN all leading hyphens MUST be removed
- AND all trailing hyphens MUST be removed
- Example: "  Foo  " → "foo" (not "-foo-")
- Example: "---bar---" → "bar"
- Example: "!!!Hello" → "hello" (exclamations removed, no leading hyphen)

**Rationale**: Slugs beginning or ending with hyphens look incomplete and may cause issues with URL parsing or routing logic.

---

### REQ-006: Function Interface and Behavior
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**User Story**: As a developer, I want a simple function signature that accepts a string and returns a slug so that it is easy to use and integrate.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN the slugify function is available in the utils module
- WHEN called with a single string parameter
- THEN it MUST return a string representing the processed slug
- AND the function MUST handle empty strings gracefully (return empty string)
- AND the function MUST handle strings that become empty after processing (return empty string)
- Example: slugify("") → ""
- Example: slugify("!!!") → "" (all characters removed)

**Rationale**: A simple, predictable interface with clear input/output behavior ensures ease of use and reduces integration errors.

---

## User Stories

### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from User Input
**Priority**: Must Have
**As a**: Content creator
**I want**: My article titles automatically converted to URL-safe slugs
**So that**: URLs are clean, readable, and SEO-friendly

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN a user enters "Hello, World!" as an article title
- WHEN the system generates a slug
- THEN the slug MUST be "hello-world"
- AND the URL becomes "/articles/hello-world"

---

### STORY-002: Handle Complex Punctuation and Spacing
**Priority**: Must Have
**As a**: System administrator
**I want**: Arbitrary text with special characters converted safely
**So that**: Generated slugs never break URL routing or file naming

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN input like "Foo__Bar  Baz!!!"
- WHEN the slugify function processes it
- THEN the output MUST be "foo-bar-baz"
- AND no special characters remain
- AND spacing is normalized to single hyphens

---

# Design: Slugify String Utility Function

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-28

## Summary

Add a pure `slugify` function to the existing utils module that transforms arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs through a sequence of normalization steps: lowercase conversion, space/underscore replacement with hyphens, character whitelist enforcement (a-z, 0-9, hyphen only), hyphen consolidation, and leading/trailing hyphen trimming. The implementation uses standard JavaScript string methods and regex for efficient, dependency-free processing.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph utils.ts
        greet["greet()"]
        add["add()"]
        slugify["slugify()"]
    end

    Input["Input String"] --> slugify
    slugify --> Output["URL-safe slug"]
```

The `slugify` function follows the existing pure function pattern in `utils.ts` with no external dependencies.

**Data Flow**:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Input: 'Hello, World!'"] --> B["1. toLowerCase()"]
    B --> C["'hello, world!'"]
    C --> D["2. Replace spaces/underscores with hyphens"]
    D --> E["'hello,-world!'"]
    E --> F["3. Remove non-whitelisted chars"]
    F --> G["'hello-world'"]
    G --> H["4. Collapse consecutive hyphens"]
    H --> I["'hello-world'"]
    I --> J["5. Trim leading/trailing hyphens"]
    J --> K["Output: 'hello-world'"]
```

## Contracts

| Contract | Producer | Consumer | Required Fields Or Outputs |
|----------|----------|----------|----------------------------|
| slugify function signature | utils.ts | Application code | `slugify(text: string): string` |
| Slug format guarantee | slugify | URL routing, database | Contains only `[a-z0-9-]`, no leading/trailing hyphens, no consecutive hyphens |

## Component Plan

| # | Component | Description | Files Changed |
|---|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| T1 | slugify function | Implement the slugify transformation function with JSDoc | `src/utils.ts` |
| T2 | Unit tests | Add comprehensive tests covering all requirements and edge cases | `src/utils.test.ts` |

## Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1] - Function implementation has no dependencies

**Dependencies**:

- T2 -> T1 (Interface: tests import and validate the slugify function)

**Critical Path**: T1 -> T2

## Validation Plan

| Behavior Or Contract | Failure Mode Covered | Test Type | Evidence Or Command |
|----------------------|----------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| REQ-001: Lowercase conversion | Mixed case not normalized | unit | `bun test` - verify "Hello" becomes "hello" |
| REQ-002: Space/underscore replacement | Spaces or underscores remain in output | unit | `bun test` - verify "Foo Bar" and "Foo_Bar" become "foo-bar" |
| REQ-003: Character whitelist | Invalid characters pass through | unit | `bun test` - verify "Hello, World!" becomes "hello-world" |
| REQ-004: Hyphen consolidation | Multiple consecutive hyphens in output | unit | `bun test` - verify "a---b" becomes "a-b" |
| REQ-005: Leading/trailing hyphen removal | Slug starts or ends with hyphen | unit | `bun test` - verify "  Foo  " becomes "foo" |
| REQ-006: Empty string handling | Error or undefined on empty input | unit | `bun test` - verify "" returns "" and "!!!" returns "" |
| All examples from requirements | Regression against documented behavior | unit | `bun test` - all 11 examples from requirements table |

## Documentation Impact

| Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale |
|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| edit | modules.md | Utils | index.md:modules | Add slugify to Utils module description |

## Open Risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Regex edge cases with unusual Unicode | LOW | Explicitly out of scope per requirements; function handles ASCII only |

# Design Decisions: Slugify String Utility Function

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Created**: 2026-07-28

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | Function location | Add to existing `src/utils.ts` | Follows existing codebase pattern where utility functions are co-located in a single module | Create new `src/slugify.ts` module (rejected: over-engineering for single function) |
| D2 | Implementation approach | Use regex and built-in string methods | No external dependencies required; matches project's "no external dependencies beyond Bun built-ins" pattern | Use third-party slugify library (rejected: unnecessary dependency) |
| D3 | Transformation order | lowercase -> replace spaces/underscores -> remove invalid chars -> collapse hyphens -> trim | Order ensures correct handling of edge cases like "Foo  Bar" (double space) | Alternative orders could produce incorrect results for edge cases |
| D4 | Regex for character removal | `/[^a-z0-9-]/g` | Simple, readable pattern that matches the whitelist requirement exactly | Multiple replace calls (rejected: less efficient) |
| D5 | Hyphen collapse regex | `/-+/g` with replace to single hyphen | Handles any number of consecutive hyphens in one operation | Loop-based approach (rejected: regex is cleaner) |
| D6 | Test structure | Add tests to existing describe block in utils.test.ts | Follows existing test co-location pattern | Separate test file (rejected: inconsistent with existing pattern) |

---

| Module location | src/utils.ts | KB modules.md | Existing utility module for pure functions |
| Code style | JSDoc comments, camelCase functions | KB patterns.md | Matches existing codebase conventions |
| Dependencies | None (built-in only) | KB patterns.md | "No external dependencies beyond Bun built-ins" |

    10→# Feature Requirements: Slugify String Utility Function
    11→
    12→## Overview
    13→
    14→**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
    15→
    16→**Description**: A reusable string utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs by applying a series of normalization and sanitization rules.
    17→
    18→**Business Value**: Enables consistent generation of clean, readable URL slugs from user-provided or system-generated text, improving SEO, readability, and consistency across the application.
    19→
    20→## Requirements
    21→
    22→### REQ-001: Text Normalization to Lowercase
    23→**Priority**: Must Have
    24→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    25→**User Story**: As a developer, I want all input text converted to lowercase so that slugs are consistently formatted regardless of input casing.
    26→
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- GIVEN any input string with mixed case characters
    29→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    30→- THEN all alphabetic characters MUST be converted to lowercase
    31→- Example: "Hello, World!" → contains "hello" and "world" in output
    32→
    33→**Rationale**: Lowercase ensures consistency and follows common URL slug conventions used in web applications and SEO best practices.
    34→
    35→---
    36→
    37→### REQ-002: Space and Underscore Replacement
    38→**Priority**: Must Have
    39→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    40→**User Story**: As a developer, I want spaces and underscores replaced with hyphens so that slugs use standard URL-friendly separators.
    41→
    42→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    43→- GIVEN input text containing spaces (U+0020) or underscores (_)
    44→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    45→- THEN all spaces MUST be replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    46→- AND all underscores MUST be replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    47→- Example: "Foo Bar" → "foo-bar"
    48→- Example: "Foo_Bar" → "foo-bar"
    49→
    50→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs, preferred over spaces (which encode as %20) and underscores for readability and SEO.
    51→
    52→---
    53→
    54→### REQ-003: Character Whitelist Enforcement
    55→**Priority**: Must Have
    56→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    57→**User Story**: As a developer, I want only safe characters retained so that the resulting slug is valid for use in URLs without encoding.

   136→- Interactive: emit `waiting_for_user` on `implementation` with prompt "Task review failed after retry. Repair, Skip task, or Stop?" and context about the failing task unit. Then emit `implementation` waiting with `task_unit: "{TASK_UNIT_IDS}"` and `reason: "review_retry_exhausted"`. STOP with `/build {FEATURE_ID}` resume instructions.
   137→- AFK: if an explicit skip policy exists, record the skipped `TASK_UNIT_IDS` as release follow-ups; otherwise emit parent `implementation` failed only because no skip/repair path remains.
   138→
   139→#### Pipelining Rules
   140→
   141→1. **Never two builders concurrently** (serial mode). At most one task-builder may be in flight at any time in the default serial-pipelined path. The only concurrency is one reviewer alongside one builder on different units.
   142→2. **Never reviewer and builder on the same unit.** A unit's reviewer dispatches only after that unit's builder completes.
   143→3. **Dependency gate.** A unit whose `depends_on` contains task IDs from unit k must not begin building until k's reviewer returns `SUCCESS`.
   144→4. **Failure isolation.** When a pipelined reviewer(k) fails, wait for the in-flight builder(k+1) to finish, then resolve k's retry before any new dispatch.
   145→5. **Max two builders** (parallel-wave mode only). Parallel-wave mode dispatches at most two builders concurrently -- one on the primary `codeRoot`, one on a worktree `codeRoot`. Never three or more.
   146→6. **Parallel mode requires GIT_COMMIT=true and clean tree.** Without atomic commits the integration rebase has nothing to replay. A dirty working tree prevents worktree creation.
   147→7. **Overlapping file lists never concurrent.** If two units' task file lists share any source file path, they MUST NOT be in flight together — this applies to pipelined reviewer(k) ∥ builder(k+1) dispatch as well as parallel-wave builders. Fall back to strictly serial dispatch for those units.
   148→8. **Serial fallback.** When in doubt about preconditions, file overlap, or worktree health, fall back to the serial pipelined path. Parallel-wave is an optimization, not a requirement.
   149→9. **Emit namespacing unchanged.** Both primary and secondary builders emit with the same `task-builder:` step prefix. The `--unit` parameter distinguishes their events.
   150→10. **Default no-commit builds are serial.** When `GIT_COMMIT=false`, parallel groups in `tasks.md` describe dependency windows, but builder execution stays serial-pipelined because there is no atomic commit to replay from a worktree.
   151→
   152→#### Parallel-Wave Mode
   153→
   154→When ALL of the following preconditions are met, dispatch two builders concurrently instead of one:
   155→
   156→1. `GIT_COMMIT` is `true`.
   157→2. The working tree at `codeRoot` is clean (no unstaged or uncommitted changes).
   158→3. The ready set contains 2+ units with no mutual dependency (neither unit's `depends_on` includes the other's task IDs).
   159→4. The two candidate units' task file lists have no overlapping source file paths.
   160→
   161→**Trigger**: At the start of each dispatch cycle, before selecting a serial unit, compute the current ready wave. If at least two ready units are mutually independent and file-disjoint, dispatch the first unit as primary builder(k) on `codeRoot` and the second unit as secondary builder(k+1) on a worktree `codeRoot` in a single message.
   162→
   163→If fewer than two ready units qualify, use the standard serial-pipelined dispatch.
   164→
   165→**Dispatch**:
   166→
   167→Task tool:
   168→subagent_type: rp1-dev:task-builder
   169→prompt:
   170→FEATURE_ID={FEATURE_ID}, KB_ROOT={kbRoot}, WORK_ROOT={workRoot}, CODE_ROOT={codeRoot}, TASK_IDS={TASK_UNIT_IDS_K}, GIT_COMMIT={GIT_COMMIT}, WORKFLOW=build, RUN_ID={RUN_ID}
   171→
   172→Task tool:
   173→subagent_type: rp1-dev:task-builder
   174→prompt:
   175→FEATURE_ID={FEATURE_ID}, KB_ROOT={kbRoot}, WORK_ROOT={workRoot}, CODE_ROOT={worktreePath}, TASK_IDS={TASK_UNIT_IDS_K1}, GIT_COMMIT={GIT_COMMIT}, WORKFLOW=build, RUN_ID={RUN_ID}
   176→
   177→Wait for both builders to complete. Dispatch reviewer(k) on the primary `codeRoot` before integrating the secondary worktree. If reviewer(k) fails or is malformed, abandon the secondary worktree, retry or escalate k per the Reviewer Failure sections, and rebuild k+1 later from the serial path after k passes. If reviewer(k) succeeds, add k's task IDs to `COMPLETED_UNIT_TASK_IDS`, then integrate the secondary worktree per `references/parallel-builders.md` and dispatch reviewer(k+1) on the primary `codeRoot`.
   178→
   179→**Integration order**: After both builders finish and reviewer(k) succeeds, integrate the worktree branch (k+1) onto the primary branch per the Integration section in `references/parallel-builders.md`. If integration fails, apply the Conflict Fallback procedure (discard worktree, rebuild k+1 serially). Then dispatch reviewer(k+1) using the standard serial or pipelined path.
   180→
   181→See `references/parallel-builders.md` for the full worktree lifecycle protocol: creation, CODE_ROOT routing, integration, conflict fallback, cleanup, and failure handling.
   182→
   183→### §4.4 Post-Build
   184→
   185→Documentation tasks from `TASK_PLAN.documentation_tasks`:
   186→
   187→- Complete only through a declared supported workflow.
   188→- Current build has no declared docs implementation workflow; create `documentation_followups` from each docs task with `id`, `title`, `target`, `acceptance_refs`, `dependencies`, and `blocks_release = false`.
   189→- Carry `documentation_followups` into readiness/release `manual_items`.
   190→- Do not spawn undeclared documentation agents.
   191→
   192→### §4.5 Cleanup Manifest Generation
   193→
   194→After builders, reviewers, and documentation follow-up collection finish, generate the durable cleanup handoff before verification:
   195→
   196→```bash
   197→rp1 agent-tools change-manifest generate \
   198→  --code-root "{codeRoot}" \
   199→  --out "{workRoot}/features/{FEATURE_ID}/change-manifest-001.json" \
   200→  --status-out "{workRoot}/features/{FEATURE_ID}/change-manifest-status.json" \
   201→  --source build \
   202→  --baseline "{workRoot}/features/{FEATURE_ID}/change-manifest-baseline.json"
   203→```
   204→
   205→Parse the `ToolResult` envelope into `cleanup_manifest_result`. If `data.status == "created"` with `files > 0` and `ownedLineCount > 0`, `comment-cleaner` may participate using `data.manifestPath`. If `data.status == "skipped"`, preserve `statusPath`/`skipReason` for the aggregator. On failure: set skipped with `skipReason: "change_manifest_generate_failed"`, `files: 0`, `ownedLineCount: 0`.
   206→
   207→### §4.6 Verification And Readiness
   208→
   209→#### Step 1 — Resolve comment-cleaner participation
   210→
   211→Evaluate the cleanup manifest result BEFORE dispatching any verification agent. Comment-cleaner participates only when ALL of: `cleanup_manifest_result.data.status == "created"`, `cleanup_manifest_result.data.files > 0`, `cleanup_manifest_result.data.ownedLineCount > 0`, and `cleanup_manifest_result.data.manifestPath` is present. Do not dispatch comment-cleaner with branch, unstaged, commit-range, base-branch, mode, or commit parameters; the generated manifest is the only safe cleanup boundary.

   216→
   217→Emit all dispatch blocks below back-to-back in one message, with no text between them — prose between blocks breaks the parallel dispatch. Always include `code-checker` and `feature-verifier`. Include `comment-cleaner` only when Step 1 resolved it as participating; when not, omit its block entirely. No prose, conditionals, or explanatory text may appear between dispatch blocks.

   221→prompt:

   246→
   247→Readiness release behavior:
   248→
   249→- PASS/proceed: release may start.
   250→- WARN/proceed_with_notes: release may start with warnings/manual notes visible.
   251→- FAIL/return_to_implementation: keep parent `implementation` running for planned repair or waiting for a user decision.

Repair, Add Task, Review feedback from Arcade, or Stop?" and readiness context (status, blocker/warning/manual-item counts, readiness artifact path). Then emit `implementation` waiting with `readiness_status`. STOP with `/build {FEATURE_ID}` resume instructions.

   284→### Git Operations (conditional)

   288→## §PHASE-4: Release

   290→**Skip if**: `START_PHASE` is after `release`.
   291→
   292→**Resume checkpoint**: If `WAITING_PHASE.phase == "release"`, inspect the latest parent waiting/status event from `WORKFLOW_STATE.recent_events`:

     9→
    10→# Feature Requirements: Slugify String Utility Function
    11→
    12→## Overview
    13→
    14→**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
    15→
    16→**Description**: A reusable string utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs by applying a series of normalization and sanitization rules.
    17→
    18→**Business Value**: Enables consistent generation of clean, readable URL slugs from user-provided or system-generated text, improving SEO, readability, and consistency across the application.
    19→
    20→## Requirements
    21→
    22→### REQ-001: Text Normalization to Lowercase
    23→**Priority**: Must Have
    24→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    25→**User Story**: As a developer, I want all input text converted to lowercase so that slugs are consistently formatted regardless of input casing.
    26→
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- GIVEN any input string with mixed case characters
    29→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    30→- THEN all alphabetic characters MUST be converted to lowercase
    31→- Example: "Hello, World!" → contains "hello" and "world" in output
    32→
    33→**Rationale**: Lowercase ensures consistency and follows common URL slug conventions used in web applications and SEO best practices.
    34→
    35→---
    36→
    37→### REQ-002: Space and Underscore Replacement
    38→**Priority**: Must Have
    39→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    40→**User Story**: As a developer, I want spaces and underscores replaced with hyphens so that slugs use standard URL-friendly separators.
    41→
    42→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    43→- GIVEN input text containing spaces (U+0020) or underscores (_)
    44→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    45→- THEN all spaces MUST be replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    46→- AND all underscores MUST be replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    47→- Example: "Foo Bar" → "foo-bar"
    48→- Example: "Foo_Bar" → "foo-bar"
    49→
    50→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs, preferred over spaces (which encode as %20) and underscores for readability and SEO.
    51→
    52→---
    53→
    54→### REQ-003: Character Whitelist Enforcement
    55→**Priority**: Must Have
    56→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    57→**User Story**: As a developer, I want only safe characters retained so that the resulting slug is valid for use in URLs without encoding.
    58→
    59→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    60→- GIVEN input text containing any characters
    61→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    62→- THEN only the following characters MUST be retained:
    63→  - Lowercase letters (a-z)
    64→  - Numbers (0-9)
    65→  - Hyphens (-)
    66→- AND all other characters MUST be removed
    67→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
    68→- Example: "Foo@Bar#123" → "foobar123" (@ and # removed)
    69→
    70→**Rationale**: Restricting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures the slug is safe for URLs, file systems, and database identifiers without special encoding.
    71→
    72→---
    73→
    74→### REQ-004: Hyphen Consolidation
    75→**Priority**: Must Have
    76→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    77→**User Story**: As a developer, I want consecutive hyphens collapsed to a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.
    78→
    79→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    80→- GIVEN text that would produce multiple consecutive hyphens after character removal and replacement
    81→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    82→- THEN all sequences of 2 or more consecutive hyphens MUST be replaced with a single hyphen
    83→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
    84→- Example: "Foo  Bar" → "foo-bar" (two spaces become one hyphen)
    85→- Example: "Hello,,,World" → "helloworld" (commas removed, no extra hyphens)
    86→
    87→**Rationale**: Multiple consecutive hyphens reduce readability and appear unprofessional in URLs.
    88→
    89→---
    90→
    91→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal
    92→**Priority**: Must Have
    93→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    94→**User Story**: As a developer, I want leading and trailing hyphens removed so that slugs start and end with meaningful content.
    95→
    96→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    97→- GIVEN text that would produce hyphens at the beginning or end after processing
    98→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    99→- THEN all leading hyphens MUST be removed
   100→- AND all trailing hyphens MUST be removed
   101→- Example: "  Foo  " → "foo" (not "-foo-")
   102→- Example: "---bar---" → "bar"
   103→- Example: "!!!Hello" → "hello" (exclamations removed, no leading hyphen)
   104→
   105→**Rationale**: Slugs beginning or ending with hyphens look incomplete and may cause issues with URL parsing or routing logic.
   106→
   107→---
   108→
   109→### REQ-006: Function Interface and Behavior
   110→**Priority**: Must Have
   111→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
   112→**User Story**: As a developer, I want a simple function signature that accepts a string and returns a slug so that it is easy to use and integrate.
   113→
   114→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   115→- GIVEN the slugify function is available in the utils module
   116→- WHEN called with a single string parameter
   117→- THEN it MUST return a string representing the processed slug
   118→- AND the function MUST handle empty strings gracefully (return empty string)
   119→- AND the function MUST handle strings that become empty after processing (return empty string)
   120→- Example: slugify("") → ""
   121→- Example: slugify("!!!") → "" (all characters removed)
   122→
   123→**Rationale**: A simple, predictable interface with clear input/output behavior ensures ease of use and reduces integration errors.
   124→
   125→---
   126→
   127→## User Stories
   128→
   129→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from User Input
   130→**Priority**: Must Have
   131→**As a**: Content creator
   132→**I want**: My article titles automatically converted to URL-safe slugs
   133→**So that**: URLs are clean, readable, and SEO-friendly
   134→
   135→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   136→- GIVEN a user enters "Hello, World!" as an article title
   137→- WHEN the system generates a slug
   138→- THEN the slug MUST be "hello-world"
   139→- AND the URL becomes "/articles/hello-world"
   140→
   141→---
   142→
   143→### STORY-002: Handle Complex Punctuation and Spacing
   144→**Priority**: Must Have
   145→**As a**: System administrator
   146→**I want**: Arbitrary text with special characters converted safely
   147→**So that**: Generated slugs never break URL routing or file naming
   148→
   149→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   150→- GIVEN input like "Foo__Bar  Baz!!!"
   151→- WHEN the slugify function processes it
   152→- THEN the output MUST be "foo-bar-baz"
   153→- AND no special characters remain
   154→- AND spacing is normalized to single hyphens
   155→
   156→---
   157→
   158→### STORY-003: Prevent Empty or Invalid Slugs
   159→**Priority**: Should Have
   160→**As a**: Developer
   161→**I want**: Empty or invalid input handled gracefully
   162→**So that**: The system doesn't generate broken URLs
   163→
   164→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   165→- GIVEN input that contains only special characters ("!!!", "@@@")
   166→- WHEN the slugify function processes it
   167→- THEN it MUST return an empty string
   168→- AND the calling code can detect this and apply fallback logic
   169→
   170→---
   171→
   172→## Examples
   173→
   174→| Input | Expected Output |
   175→|-------|-----------------|
   176→| "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" |
   177→| "Foo__Bar" | "foo-bar" |
   178→| "  Foo  " | "foo" |
   179→| "a---b" | "a-b" |
   180→| "Test 123" | "test-123" |
   181→| "CamelCaseText" | "camelcasetext" |
   182→| "Multi   Spaces" | "multi-spaces" |
   183→| "Special!@#Chars" | "specialchars" |
   184→| "" | "" |
   185→| "!!!" | "" |
   186→| "---" | "" |
   187→
   188→## Success Criteria
   189→
   190→The feature is considered complete when:
   191→
   192→1. A `slugify(text: string): string` function exists in the utility module
   193→2. All transformation rules (lowercase, character whitelisting, hyphen normalization, trimming) are correctly implemented
   194→3. All examples listed above produce the expected output
   195→4. The function handles edge cases (empty strings, all-special-characters, whitespace-only) correctly
   196→5. Unit tests validate all requirements and user stories
   197→6. The function is exported from the utils module for use by other components
   198→
   199→## Out of Scope
   200→
   201→The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
   202→
   203→- Unicode normalization (e.g., converting accented characters to ASCII equivalents)
   204→- Custom separator characters (only hyphen is supported)
   205→- Locale-specific transformations
   206→- Length limits or truncation
   207→- Uniqueness guarantees (slug collision handling)
   208→- Database persistence or slug management
   209→- Integration with specific routing or CMS systems
   210→
   211→## Dependencies
   212→
   213→- Bun runtime environment
   214→- TypeScript language support
   215→- Existing `src/utils.ts` module structure
   216→
   217→## Assumptions
   218→
   219→1. Input text is provided as a JavaScript/TypeScript string
   220→2. The target environment supports modern JavaScript string methods
   221→3. The function will be used synchronously (no async behavior required)
   222→4. Performance for strings up to several hundred characters is acceptable with straightforward string operations
   223→5. The calling code is responsible for handling empty string results appropriately
   224→
   225→## AFK Mode Analysis
   226→

   229→### Decision Log

   231→**Decision Point**: PRD Association
   232→**Choice**: No PRD associated

   236→**Choice**: Focused on basic ASCII slug generation without Unicode normalization
   237→**Rationale**: The provided examples use only ASCII characters. Unicode handling (e.g., "café" → "cafe") was not mentioned in the input requirements, so it is treated as out of scope to avoid over-engineering.
   238→
   239→**Decision Point**: Empty String Handling
   240→**Choice**: Return empty string for empty or all-invalid input
   241→**Rationale**: Conservative default behavior. Allows calling code to detect invalid input and apply fallback logic (e.g., auto-generated IDs) without throwing errors.
   242→
   243→**Decision Point**: Character Whitelist Definition

   246→

   249→**Rationale**: Ensures cases like "Foo  Bar" (double space) and "Foo__Bar" (double underscore) both become "foo-bar" with a single hyphen separator.

/**
 * Add two numbers.
 */
export function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  return a + b;
}

/**
 * Transform arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs.
 *
 * Applies the following transformations:
 * 1. Converts to lowercase
 * 2. Replaces spaces and underscores with hyphens
 * 3. Removes all characters except lowercase letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens
 * 4. Collapses consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen
 * 5. Removes leading and trailing hyphens
 *
 * @param text - The input text to slugify
 * @returns A URL-safe slug containing only [a-z0-9-], or empty string if input becomes empty after processing
 *
 * @example
 * slugify("Hello, World!") // returns "hello-world"
 * slugify("Foo__Bar")      // returns "foo-bar"
 * slugify("  Foo  ")       // returns "foo"
 * slugify("!!!")           // returns ""
 */
export function slugify(text: string): string {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[\s_]+/g, '-')
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, '')
    .replace(/-+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');
}

    12→## Overview
    13→
    14→**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
    15→
    16→**Description**: A reusable string utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs by applying a series of normalization and sanitization rules.
    17→
    18→**Business Value**: Enables consistent generation of clean, readable URL slugs from user-provided or system-generated text, improving SEO, readability, and consistency across the application.
    19→
    20→## Requirements
    21→
    22→### REQ-001: Text Normalization to Lowercase
    23→**Priority**: Must Have
    24→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    25→**User Story**: As a developer, I want all input text converted to lowercase so that slugs are consistently formatted regardless of input casing.
    26→
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- GIVEN any input string with mixed case characters
    29→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    30→- THEN all alphabetic characters MUST be converted to lowercase
    31→- Example: "Hello, World!" → contains "hello" and "world" in output
    32→
    33→**Rationale**: Lowercase ensures consistency and follows common URL slug conventions used in web applications and SEO best practices.
    34→
    35→---
    36→
    37→### REQ-002: Space and Underscore Replacement
    38→**Priority**: Must Have
    39→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    40→**User Story**: As a developer, I want spaces and underscores replaced with hyphens so that slugs use standard URL-friendly separators.
    41→
    42→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    43→- GIVEN input text containing spaces (U+0020) or underscores (_)
    44→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    45→- THEN all spaces MUST be replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    46→- AND all underscores MUST be replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    47→- Example: "Foo Bar" → "foo-bar"
    48→- Example: "Foo_Bar" → "foo-bar"
    49→
    50→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs, preferred over spaces (which encode as %20) and underscores for readability and SEO.
    51→
    52→---
    53→
    54→### REQ-003: Character Whitelist Enforcement
    55→**Priority**: Must Have
    56→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    57→**User Story**: As a developer, I want only safe characters retained so that the resulting slug is valid for use in URLs without encoding.
    58→
    59→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    60→- GIVEN input text containing any characters
    61→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    62→- THEN only the following characters MUST be retained:
    63→  - Lowercase letters (a-z)
    64→  - Numbers (0-9)
    65→  - Hyphens (-)
    66→- AND all other characters MUST be removed
    67→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
    68→- Example: "Foo@Bar#123" → "foobar123" (@ and # removed)
    69→
    70→**Rationale**: Restricting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures the slug is safe for URLs, file systems, and database identifiers without special encoding.
    71→

    73→
    74→### REQ-004: Hyphen Consolidation
    75→**Priority**: Must Have
    76→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module

    78→
    79→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    80→- GIVEN text that would produce multiple consecutive hyphens after character removal and replacement
    81→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    82→- THEN all sequences of 2 or more consecutive hyphens MUST be replaced with a single hyphen
    83→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
    84→- Example: "Foo  Bar" → "foo-bar" (two spaces become one hyphen)
    85→- Example: "Hello,,,World" → "helloworld" (commas removed, no extra hyphens)
    86→
    87→**Rationale**: Multiple consecutive hyphens reduce readability and appear unprofessional in URLs.
    88→
    89→---
    90→
    91→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal
    92→**Priority**: Must Have
    93→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    94→**User Story**: As a developer, I want leading and trailing hyphens removed so that slugs start and end with meaningful content.
    95→
    96→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    97→- GIVEN text that would produce hyphens at the beginning or end after processing
    98→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    99→- THEN all leading hyphens MUST be removed

   102→- Example: "---bar---" → "bar"
   103→- Example: "!!!Hello" → "hello" (exclamations removed, no leading hyphen)

   105→**Rationale**: Slugs beginning or ending with hyphens look incomplete and may cause issues with URL parsing or routing logic.

     4→
     5→/**
     6→ * Greet someone by name.

     8→export function greet(name: string): string {

    11→

    13→ * Add two numbers.

    15→export function add(a: number, b: number): number {
    16→  return a + b;

    19→/**
    20→ * Transform arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs.
    21→ *
    22→ * Applies the following transformations:
    23→ * 1. Converts to lowercase
    24→ * 2. Replaces spaces and underscores with hyphens
    25→ * 3. Removes all characters except lowercase letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and hyphens
    26→ * 4. Collapses consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen
    27→ * 5. Removes leading and trailing hyphens
    28→ *
    29→ * @param text - The input text to slugify
    30→ * @returns A URL-safe slug containing only [a-z0-9-], or empty string if input becomes empty after processing
    31→ *
    32→ * @example
    33→ * slugify("Hello, World!") // returns "hello-world"
    34→ * slugify("Foo__Bar")      // returns "foo-bar"
    35→ * slugify("  Foo  ")       // returns "foo"
    36→ * slugify("!!!")           // returns ""
    37→ */
    38→export function slugify(text: string): string {
    39→  return text
    40→    .toLowerCase()
    41→    .replace(/[\s_]+/g, '-')
    42→    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, '')
    43→    .replace(/-+/g, '-')
    44→    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');
    45→}

    10→# Feature Requirements: Slugify String Utility Function
    11→
    12→## Overview
    13→
    14→**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
    15→
    16→**Description**: A reusable string utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs by applying a series of normalization and sanitization rules.
    17→
    18→**Business Value**: Enables consistent generation of clean, readable URL slugs from user-provided or system-generated text, improving SEO, readability, and consistency across the application.
    19→
    20→## Requirements
    21→
    22→### REQ-001: Text Normalization to Lowercase
    23→**Priority**: Must Have
    24→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    25→**User Story**: As a developer, I want all input text converted to lowercase so that slugs are consistently formatted regardless of input casing.
    26→
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- GIVEN any input string with mixed case characters
    29→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    30→- THEN all alphabetic characters MUST be converted to lowercase
    31→- Example: "Hello, World!" → contains "hello" and "world" in output
    32→
    33→**Rationale**: Lowercase ensures consistency and follows common URL slug conventions used in web applications and SEO best practices.
    34→
    35→---
    36→
    37→### REQ-002: Space and Underscore Replacement
    38→**Priority**: Must Have
    39→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    40→**User Story**: As a developer, I want spaces and underscores replaced with hyphens so that slugs use standard URL-friendly separators.
    41→
    42→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    43→- GIVEN input text containing spaces (U+0020) or underscores (_)
    44→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    45→- THEN all spaces MUST be replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    46→- AND all underscores MUST be replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    47→- Example: "Foo Bar" → "foo-bar"
    48→- Example: "Foo_Bar" → "foo-bar"
    49→
    50→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs, preferred over spaces (which encode as %20) and underscores for readability and SEO.
    51→
    52→---
    53→
    54→### REQ-003: Character Whitelist Enforcement
    55→**Priority**: Must Have
    56→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    57→**User Story**: As a developer, I want only safe characters retained so that the resulting slug is valid for use in URLs without encoding.
    58→
    59→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    60→- GIVEN input text containing any characters
    61→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    62→- THEN only the following characters MUST be retained:
    63→  - Lowercase letters (a-z)
    64→  - Numbers (0-9)
    65→  - Hyphens (-)
    66→- AND all other characters MUST be removed
    67→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
    68→- Example: "Foo@Bar#123" → "foobar123" (@ and # removed)
    69→
    70→**Rationale**: Restricting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures the slug is safe for URLs, file systems, and database identifiers without special encoding.
    71→
    72→---
    73→
    74→### REQ-004: Hyphen Consolidation
    75→**Priority**: Must Have
    76→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    77→**User Story**: As a developer, I want consecutive hyphens collapsed to a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.
    78→
    79→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    80→- GIVEN text that would produce multiple consecutive hyphens after character removal and replacement
    81→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    82→- THEN all sequences of 2 or more consecutive hyphens MUST be replaced with a single hyphen
    83→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
    84→- Example: "Foo  Bar" → "foo-bar" (two spaces become one hyphen)
    85→- Example: "Hello,,,World" → "helloworld" (commas removed, no extra hyphens)
    86→
    87→**Rationale**: Multiple consecutive hyphens reduce readability and appear unprofessional in URLs.
    88→
    89→---
    90→
    91→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal
    92→**Priority**: Must Have
    93→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    94→**User Story**: As a developer, I want leading and trailing hyphens removed so that slugs start and end with meaningful content.
    95→
    96→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    97→- GIVEN text that would produce hyphens at the beginning or end after processing
    98→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    99→- THEN all leading hyphens MUST be removed
   100→- AND all trailing hyphens MUST be removed
   101→- Example: "  Foo  " → "foo" (not "-foo-")
   102→- Example: "---bar---" → "bar"
   103→- Example: "!!!Hello" → "hello" (exclamations removed, no leading hyphen)
   104→
   105→**Rationale**: Slugs beginning or ending with hyphens look incomplete and may cause issues with URL parsing or routing logic.
   106→
   107→---
   108→
   109→### REQ-006: Function Interface and Behavior
   110→**Priority**: Must Have
   111→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
   112→**User Story**: As a developer, I want a simple function signature that accepts a string and returns a slug so that it is easy to use and integrate.
   113→
   114→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   115→- GIVEN the slugify function is available in the utils module
   116→- WHEN called with a single string parameter
   117→- THEN it MUST return a string representing the processed slug
   118→- AND the function MUST handle empty strings gracefully (return empty string)
   119→- AND the function MUST handle strings that become empty after processing (return empty string)
   120→- Example: slugify("") → ""
   121→- Example: slugify("!!!") → "" (all characters removed)
   122→
   123→**Rationale**: A simple, predictable interface with clear input/output behavior ensures ease of use and reduces integration errors.
   124→
   125→---
   126→
   127→## User Stories
   128→
   129→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from User Input
   130→**Priority**: Must Have
   131→**As a**: Content creator
   132→**I want**: My article titles automatically converted to URL-safe slugs
   133→**So that**: URLs are clean, readable, and SEO-friendly
   134→
   135→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   136→- GIVEN a user enters "Hello, World!" as an article title
   137→- WHEN the system generates a slug
   138→- THEN the slug MUST be "hello-world"
   139→- AND the URL becomes "/articles/hello-world"
   140→
   141→---
   142→
   143→### STORY-002: Handle Complex Punctuation and Spacing
   144→**Priority**: Must Have
   145→**As a**: System administrator
   146→**I want**: Arbitrary text with special characters converted safely
   147→**So that**: Generated slugs never break URL routing or file naming
   148→
   149→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   150→- GIVEN input like "Foo__Bar  Baz!!!"
   151→- WHEN the slugify function processes it
   152→- THEN the output MUST be "foo-bar-baz"
   153→- AND no special characters remain
   154→- AND spacing is normalized to single hyphens
   155→
   156→---
   157→
   158→### STORY-003: Prevent Empty or Invalid Slugs
   159→**Priority**: Should Have
   160→**As a**: Developer
   161→**I want**: Empty or invalid input handled gracefully
   162→**So that**: The system doesn't generate broken URLs
   163→
   164→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   165→- GIVEN input that contains only special characters ("!!!", "@@@")
   166→- WHEN the slugify function processes it
   167→- THEN it MUST return an empty string
   168→- AND the calling code can detect this and apply fallback logic
   169→
   170→---
   171→
   172→## Examples
   173→
   174→| Input | Expected Output |
   175→|-------|-----------------|
   176→| "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" |
   177→| "Foo__Bar" | "foo-bar" |
   178→| "  Foo  " | "foo" |
   179→| "a---b" | "a-b" |
   180→| "Test 123" | "test-123" |
   181→| "CamelCaseText" | "camelcasetext" |
   182→| "Multi   Spaces" | "multi-spaces" |
   183→| "Special!@#Chars" | "specialchars" |
   184→| "" | "" |
   185→| "!!!" | "" |
   186→| "---" | "" |
   187→
   188→## Success Criteria
   189→
   190→The feature is considered complete when:
   191→
   192→1. A `slugify(text: string): string` function exists in the utility module
   193→2. All transformation rules (lowercase, character whitelisting, hyphen normalization, trimming) are correctly implemented
   194→3. All examples listed above produce the expected output
   195→4. The function handles edge cases (empty strings, all-special-characters, whitespace-only) correctly
   196→5. Unit tests validate all requirements and user stories
   197→6. The function is exported from the utils module for use by other components
   198→
   199→## Out of Scope
   200→
   201→The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:
   202→
   203→- Unicode normalization (e.g., converting accented characters to ASCII equivalents)
   204→- Custom separator characters (only hyphen is supported)
   205→- Locale-specific transformations
   206→- Length limits or truncation
   207→- Uniqueness guarantees (slug collision handling)
   208→- Database persistence or slug management
   209→- Integration with specific routing or CMS systems
   210→
   211→## Dependencies
   212→
   213→- Bun runtime environment
   214→- TypeScript language support
   215→- Existing `src/utils.ts` module structure
   216→
   217→## Assumptions
   218→
   219→1. Input text is provided as a JavaScript/TypeScript string
   220→2. The target environment supports modern JavaScript string methods
   221→3. The function will be used synchronously (no async behavior required)
   222→4. Performance for strings up to several hundred characters is acceptable with straightforward string operations
   223→5. The calling code is responsible for handling empty string results appropriately
   224→
   225→## AFK Mode Analysis
   226→
   227→Since this feature was gathered in AFK mode, the following decisions were made automatically:
   228→
   229→### Decision Log
   230→
   231→**Decision Point**: PRD Association
   232→**Choice**: No PRD associated
   233→**Rationale**: No PRDs directory exists in the workspace. Proceeding with standalone feature requirements based on the provided specification.
   234→
   235→**Decision Point**: Scope Interpretation
   236→**Choice**: Focused on basic ASCII slug generation without Unicode normalization
   237→**Rationale**: The provided examples use only ASCII characters. Unicode handling (e.g., "café" → "cafe") was not mentioned in the input requirements, so it is treated as out of scope to avoid over-engineering.
   238→
   239→**Decision Point**: Empty String Handling
   240→**Choice**: Return empty string for empty or all-invalid input
   241→**Rationale**: Conservative default behavior. Allows calling code to detect invalid input and apply fallback logic (e.g., auto-generated IDs) without throwing errors.
   242→
   243→**Decision Point**: Character Whitelist Definition
   244→**Choice**: a-z, 0-9, and hyphen only
   245→**Rationale**: Matches the requirement to "drop any character that is not a letter, number, or hyphen" and aligns with standard URL slug conventions.
   246→
   247→**Decision Point**: Hyphen Collapsing Rule
   248→**Choice**: Apply after character removal and replacement
   249→**Rationale**: Ensures cases like "Foo  Bar" (double space) and "Foo__Bar" (double underscore) both become "foo-bar" with a single hyphen separator.
   250→

# Feature Requirements: Slugify String Utility Function

## Overview

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility

**Description**: A reusable string utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs by applying a series of normalization and sanitization rules.

**Business Value**: Enables consistent generation of clean, readable URL slugs from user-provided or system-generated text, improving SEO, readability, and consistency across the application.

## Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Normalization to Lowercase
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**User Story**: As a developer, I want all input text converted to lowercase so that slugs are consistently formatted regardless of input casing.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN any input string with mixed case characters
- WHEN the slugify function is called
- THEN all alphabetic characters MUST be converted to lowercase
- Example: "Hello, World!" → contains "hello" and "world" in output

**Rationale**: Lowercase ensures consistency and follows common URL slug conventions used in web applications and SEO best practices.

---

### REQ-002: Space and Underscore Replacement
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**User Story**: As a developer, I want spaces and underscores replaced with hyphens so that slugs use standard URL-friendly separators.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN input text containing spaces (U+0020) or underscores (_)
- WHEN the slugify function is called
- THEN all spaces MUST be replaced with a single hyphen (-)
- AND all underscores MUST be replaced with a single hyphen (-)
- Example: "Foo Bar" → "foo-bar"
- Example: "Foo_Bar" → "foo-bar"

**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs, preferred over spaces (which encode as %20) and underscores for readability and SEO.

---

### REQ-003: Character Whitelist Enforcement
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**User Story**: As a developer, I want only safe characters retained so that the resulting slug is valid for use in URLs without encoding.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN input text containing any characters
- WHEN the slugify function is called
- THEN only the following characters MUST be retained:
  - Lowercase letters (a-z)
  - Numbers (0-9)
  - Hyphens (-)
- AND all other characters MUST be removed
- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
- Example: "Foo@Bar#123" → "foobar123" (@ and # removed)

**Rationale**: Restricting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures the slug is safe for URLs, file systems, and database identifiers without special encoding.

---

### REQ-004: Hyphen Consolidation
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**User Story**: As a developer, I want consecutive hyphens collapsed to a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN text that would produce multiple consecutive hyphens after character removal and replacement
- WHEN the slugify function is called
- THEN all sequences of 2 or more consecutive hyphens MUST be replaced with a single hyphen
- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
- Example: "Foo  Bar" → "foo-bar" (two spaces become one hyphen)
- Example: "Hello,,,World" → "helloworld" (commas removed, no extra hyphens)

**Rationale**: Multiple consecutive hyphens reduce readability and appear unprofessional in URLs.

---

### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**User Story**: As a developer, I want leading and trailing hyphens removed so that slugs start and end with meaningful content.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN text that would produce hyphens at the beginning or end after processing
- WHEN the slugify function is called
- THEN all leading hyphens MUST be removed
- AND all trailing hyphens MUST be removed
- Example: "  Foo  " → "foo" (not "-foo-")
- Example: "---bar---" → "bar"
- Example: "!!!Hello" → "hello" (exclamations removed, no leading hyphen)

**Rationale**: Slugs beginning or ending with hyphens look incomplete and may cause issues with URL parsing or routing logic.

---

### REQ-006: Function Interface and Behavior
**Priority**: Must Have
**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
**User Story**: As a developer, I want a simple function signature that accepts a string and returns a slug so that it is easy to use and integrate.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN the slugify function is available in the utils module
- WHEN called with a single string parameter
- THEN it MUST return a string representing the processed slug
- AND the function MUST handle empty strings gracefully (return empty string)
- AND the function MUST handle strings that become empty after processing (return empty string)
- Example: slugify("") → ""
- Example: slugify("!!!") → "" (all characters removed)

**Rationale**: A simple, predictable interface with clear input/output behavior ensures ease of use and reduces integration errors.

---

## User Stories

### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from User Input
**Priority**: Must Have
**As a**: Content creator
**I want**: My article titles automatically converted to URL-safe slugs
**So that**: URLs are clean, readable, and SEO-friendly

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN a user enters "Hello, World!" as an article title
- WHEN the system generates a slug
- THEN the slug MUST be "hello-world"
- AND the URL becomes "/articles/hello-world"

---

### STORY-002: Handle Complex Punctuation and Spacing
**Priority**: Must Have
**As a**: System administrator
**I want**: Arbitrary text with special characters converted safely
**So that**: Generated slugs never break URL routing or file naming

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN input like "Foo__Bar  Baz!!!"
- WHEN the slugify function processes it
- THEN the output MUST be "foo-bar-baz"
- AND no special characters remain
- AND spacing is normalized to single hyphens

---

### STORY-003: Prevent Empty or Invalid Slugs
**Priority**: Should Have
**As a**: Developer
**I want**: Empty or invalid input handled gracefully
**So that**: The system doesn't generate broken URLs

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN input that contains only special characters ("!!!", "@@@")
- WHEN the slugify function processes it
- THEN it MUST return an empty string
- AND the calling code can detect this and apply fallback logic

---

## Examples

| Input | Expected Output |
|-------|-----------------|
| "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" |
| "Foo__Bar" | "foo-bar" |
| "  Foo  " | "foo" |
| "a---b" | "a-b" |
| "Test 123" | "test-123" |
| "CamelCaseText" | "camelcasetext" |
| "Multi   Spaces" | "multi-spaces" |
| "Special!@#Chars" | "specialchars" |
| "" | "" |
| "!!!" | "" |
| "---" | "" |

## Success Criteria

The feature is considered complete when:

1. A `slugify(text: string): string` function exists in the utility module
2. All transformation rules (lowercase, character whitelisting, hyphen normalization, trimming) are correctly implemented
3. All examples listed above produce the expected output
4. The function handles edge cases (empty strings, all-special-characters, whitespace-only) correctly
5. Unit tests validate all requirements and user stories
6. The function is exported from the utils module for use by other components

## Out of Scope

The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:

- Unicode normalization (e.g., converting accented characters to ASCII equivalents)
- Custom separator characters (only hyphen is supported)
- Locale-specific transformations
- Length limits or truncation
- Uniqueness guarantees (slug collision handling)
- Database persistence or slug management
- Integration with specific routing or CMS systems

## Dependencies

- Bun runtime environment
- TypeScript language support
- Existing `src/utils.ts` module structure

## Assumptions

1. Input text is provided as a JavaScript/TypeScript string
2. The target environment supports modern JavaScript string methods
3. The function will be used synchronously (no async behavior required)
4. Performance for strings up to several hundred characters is acceptable with straightforward string operations
5. The calling code is responsible for handling empty string results appropriately

## AFK Mode Analysis

Since this feature was gathered in AFK mode, the following decisions were made automatically:

### Decision Log

**Decision Point**: PRD Association
**Choice**: No PRD associated
**Rationale**: No PRDs directory exists in the workspace. Proceeding with standalone feature requirements based on the provided specification.

**Decision Point**: Scope Interpretation
**Choice**: Focused on basic ASCII slug generation without Unicode normalization
**Rationale**: The provided examples use only ASCII characters. Unicode handling (e.g., "café" → "cafe") was not mentioned in the input requirements, so it is treated as out of scope to avoid over-engineering.

**Decision Point**: Empty String Handling
**Choice**: Return empty string for empty or all-invalid input
**Rationale**: Conservative default behavior. Allows calling code to detect invalid input and apply fallback logic (e.g., auto-generated IDs) without throwing errors.

**Decision Point**: Character Whitelist Definition
**Choice**: a-z, 0-9, and hyphen only
**Rationale**: Matches the requirement to "drop any character that is not a letter, number, or hyphen" and aligns with standard URL slug conventions.

**Decision Point**: Hyphen Collapsing Rule
**Choice**: Apply after character removal and replacement
**Rationale**: Ensures cases like "Foo  Bar" (double space) and "Foo__Bar" (double underscore) both become "foo-bar" with a single hyphen separator.

---

    75→**Priority**: Must Have
    76→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    77→**User Story**: As a developer, I want consecutive hyphens collapsed to a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.
    78→
    79→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    80→- GIVEN text that would produce multiple consecutive hyphens after character removal and replacement
    81→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    82→- THEN all sequences of 2 or more consecutive hyphens MUST be replaced with a single hyphen
    83→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
    84→- Example: "Foo  Bar" → "foo-bar" (two spaces become one hyphen)
    85→- Example: "Hello,,,World" → "helloworld" (commas removed, no extra hyphens)
    86→
    87→**Rationale**: Multiple consecutive hyphens reduce readability and appear unprofessional in URLs.
    88→
    89→---
    90→
    91→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal
    92→**Priority**: Must Have
    93→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    94→**User Story**: As a developer, I want leading and trailing hyphens removed so that slugs start and end with meaningful content.
    95→
    96→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    97→- GIVEN text that would produce hyphens at the beginning or end after processing
    98→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    99→- THEN all leading hyphens MUST be removed
   100→- AND all trailing hyphens MUST be removed
   101→- Example: "  Foo  " → "foo" (not "-foo-")
   102→- Example: "---bar---" → "bar"
   103→- Example: "!!!Hello" → "hello" (exclamations removed, no leading hyphen)
   104→
   105→**Rationale**: Slugs beginning or ending with hyphens look incomplete and may cause issues with URL parsing or routing logic.

   110→**Priority**: Must Have
   111→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module

   113→

   115→- GIVEN the slugify function is available in the utils module
   116→- WHEN called with a single string parameter
   117→- THEN it MUST return a string representing the processed slug

   119→- AND the function MUST handle strings that become empty after processing (return empty string)
   120→- Example: slugify("") → ""
   121→- Example: slugify("!!!") → "" (all characters removed)

   123→**Rationale**: A simple, predictable interface with clear input/output behavior ensures ease of use and reduces integration errors.

# Design: Slugify String Utility Function

**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-28

## Summary

Add a pure `slugify` function to the existing utils module that transforms arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs through a sequence of normalization steps: lowercase conversion, space/underscore replacement with hyphens, character whitelist enforcement (a-z, 0-9, hyphen only), hyphen consolidation, and leading/trailing hyphen trimming. The implementation uses standard JavaScript string methods and regex for efficient, dependency-free processing.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph utils.ts
        greet["greet()"]
        add["add()"]
        slugify["slugify()"]
    end

    Input["Input String"] --> slugify
    slugify --> Output["URL-safe slug"]
```

The `slugify` function follows the existing pure function pattern in `utils.ts` with no external dependencies.

**Data Flow**:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Input: 'Hello, World!'"] --> B["1. toLowerCase()"]
    B --> C["'hello, world!'"]
    C --> D["2. Replace spaces/underscores with hyphens"]
    D --> E["'hello,-world!'"]

    12→## Overview

    14→**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
    15→
    16→**Description**: A reusable string utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs by applying a series of normalization and sanitization rules.
    17→
    18→**Business Value**: Enables consistent generation of clean, readable URL slugs from user-provided or system-generated text, improving SEO, readability, and consistency across the application.
    19→
    20→## Requirements
    21→
    22→### REQ-001: Text Normalization to Lowercase
    23→**Priority**: Must Have
    24→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    25→**User Story**: As a developer, I want all input text converted to lowercase so that slugs are consistently formatted regardless of input casing.
    26→

    28→- GIVEN any input string with mixed case characters
    29→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    30→- THEN all alphabetic characters MUST be converted to lowercase
    31→- Example: "Hello, World!" → contains "hello" and "world" in output
    32→
    33→**Rationale**: Lowercase ensures consistency and follows common URL slug conventions used in web applications and SEO best practices.
    34→
    35→---
    36→
    37→### REQ-002: Space and Underscore Replacement
    38→**Priority**: Must Have
    39→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    40→**User Story**: As a developer, I want spaces and underscores replaced with hyphens so that slugs use standard URL-friendly separators.
    41→
    42→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    43→- GIVEN input text containing spaces (U+0020) or underscores (_)
    44→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    45→- THEN all spaces MUST be replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    46→- AND all underscores MUST be replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    47→- Example: "Foo Bar" → "foo-bar"
    48→- Example: "Foo_Bar" → "foo-bar"
    49→
    50→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs, preferred over spaces (which encode as %20) and underscores for readability and SEO.
    51→
    52→---
    53→
    54→### REQ-003: Character Whitelist Enforcement
    55→**Priority**: Must Have
    56→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    57→**User Story**: As a developer, I want only safe characters retained so that the resulting slug is valid for use in URLs without encoding.
    58→
    59→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    60→- GIVEN input text containing any characters
    61→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    62→- THEN only the following characters MUST be retained:
    63→  - Lowercase letters (a-z)
    64→  - Numbers (0-9)
    65→  - Hyphens (-)
    66→- AND all other characters MUST be removed
    67→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
    68→- Example: "Foo@Bar#123" → "foobar123" (@ and # removed)
    69→
    70→**Rationale**: Restricting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures the slug is safe for URLs, file systems, and database identifiers without special encoding.
    71→
    72→---
    73→
    74→### REQ-004: Hyphen Consolidation
    75→**Priority**: Must Have
    76→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    77→**User Story**: As a developer, I want consecutive hyphens collapsed to a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.
    78→
    79→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    80→- GIVEN text that would produce multiple consecutive hyphens after character removal and replacement
    81→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    82→- THEN all sequences of 2 or more consecutive hyphens MUST be replaced with a single hyphen
    83→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
    84→- Example: "Foo  Bar" → "foo-bar" (two spaces become one hyphen)
    85→- Example: "Hello,,,World" → "helloworld" (commas removed, no extra hyphens)
    86→
    87→**Rationale**: Multiple consecutive hyphens reduce readability and appear unprofessional in URLs.
    88→
    89→---
    90→
    91→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal
    92→**Priority**: Must Have
    93→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    94→**User Story**: As a developer, I want leading and trailing hyphens removed so that slugs start and end with meaningful content.
    95→
    96→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    97→- GIVEN text that would produce hyphens at the beginning or end after processing
    98→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    99→- THEN all leading hyphens MUST be removed
   100→- AND all trailing hyphens MUST be removed
   101→- Example: "  Foo  " → "foo" (not "-foo-")
   102→- Example: "---bar---" → "bar"
   103→- Example: "!!!Hello" → "hello" (exclamations removed, no leading hyphen)
   104→
   105→**Rationale**: Slugs beginning or ending with hyphens look incomplete and may cause issues with URL parsing or routing logic.
   106→
   107→---
   108→
   109→### REQ-006: Function Interface and Behavior
   110→**Priority**: Must Have
   111→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
   112→**User Story**: As a developer, I want a simple function signature that accepts a string and returns a slug so that it is easy to use and integrate.
   113→
   114→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   115→- GIVEN the slugify function is available in the utils module
   116→- WHEN called with a single string parameter
   117→- THEN it MUST return a string representing the processed slug
   118→- AND the function MUST handle empty strings gracefully (return empty string)
   119→- AND the function MUST handle strings that become empty after processing (return empty string)
   120→- Example: slugify("") → ""
   121→- Example: slugify("!!!") → "" (all characters removed)
   122→
   123→**Rationale**: A simple, predictable interface with clear input/output behavior ensures ease of use and reduces integration errors.
   124→
   125→---
   126→
   127→## User Stories
   128→
   129→### STORY-001: Generate URL Slug from User Input
   130→**Priority**: Must Have
   131→**As a**: Content creator
   132→**I want**: My article titles automatically converted to URL-safe slugs
   133→**So that**: URLs are clean, readable, and SEO-friendly
   134→

   136→- GIVEN a user enters "Hello, World!" as an article title
   137→- WHEN the system generates a slug
   138→- THEN the slug MUST be "hello-world"
   139→- AND the URL becomes "/articles/hello-world"
   140→
   141→---
   142→
   143→### STORY-002: Handle Complex Punctuation and Spacing
   144→**Priority**: Must Have
   145→**As a**: System administrator
   146→**I want**: Arbitrary text with special characters converted safely
   147→**So that**: Generated slugs never break URL routing or file naming

   151→- WHEN the slugify function processes it
   152→- THEN the output MUST be "foo-bar-baz"
   153→- AND no special characters remain
   154→- AND spacing is normalized to single hyphens
   155→
   156→---
   157→
   158→### STORY-003: Prevent Empty or Invalid Slugs
   159→**Priority**: Should Have
   160→**As a**: Developer
   161→**I want**: Empty or invalid input handled gracefully
   162→**So that**: The system doesn't generate broken URLs

   166→- WHEN the slugify function processes it

   168→- AND the calling code can detect this and apply fallback logic
   169→
   170→---
   171→
   172→## Examples
   173→
   174→| Input | Expected Output |
   175→|-------|-----------------|

   182→| "Multi   Spaces" | "multi-spaces" |
   183→| "Special!@#Chars" | "specialchars" |
   184→| "" | "" |
   185→| "!!!" | "" |
   186→| "---" | "" |
   187→
   188→## Success Criteria
   189→
   190→The feature is considered complete when:
   191→
   192→1. A `slugify(text: string): string` function exists in the utility module
   193→2. All transformation rules (lowercase, character whitelisting, hyphen normalization, trimming) are correctly implemented

   199→## Out of Scope

   217→## Assumptions

    10→# Feature Requirements: Slugify String Utility Function
    11→
    12→## Overview
    13→
    14→**Feature ID**: slugify-utility
    15→
    16→**Description**: A reusable string utility function that transforms arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs by applying a series of normalization and sanitization rules.
    17→
    18→**Business Value**: Enables consistent generation of clean, readable URL slugs from user-provided or system-generated text, improving SEO, readability, and consistency across the application.
    19→
    20→## Requirements
    21→
    22→### REQ-001: Text Normalization to Lowercase
    23→**Priority**: Must Have
    24→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    25→**User Story**: As a developer, I want all input text converted to lowercase so that slugs are consistently formatted regardless of input casing.
    26→
    27→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    28→- GIVEN any input string with mixed case characters
    29→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    30→- THEN all alphabetic characters MUST be converted to lowercase
    31→- Example: "Hello, World!" → contains "hello" and "world" in output
    32→
    33→**Rationale**: Lowercase ensures consistency and follows common URL slug conventions used in web applications and SEO best practices.
    34→
    35→---
    36→
    37→### REQ-002: Space and Underscore Replacement
    38→**Priority**: Must Have
    39→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    40→**User Story**: As a developer, I want spaces and underscores replaced with hyphens so that slugs use standard URL-friendly separators.
    41→
    42→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    43→- GIVEN input text containing spaces (U+0020) or underscores (_)
    44→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    45→- THEN all spaces MUST be replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    46→- AND all underscores MUST be replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    47→- Example: "Foo Bar" → "foo-bar"
    48→- Example: "Foo_Bar" → "foo-bar"
    49→
    50→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the standard word separator in URL slugs, preferred over spaces (which encode as %20) and underscores for readability and SEO.
    51→
    52→---
    53→
    54→### REQ-003: Character Whitelist Enforcement
    55→**Priority**: Must Have
    56→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    57→**User Story**: As a developer, I want only safe characters retained so that the resulting slug is valid for use in URLs without encoding.
    58→
    59→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    60→- GIVEN input text containing any characters
    61→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    62→- THEN only the following characters MUST be retained:
    63→  - Lowercase letters (a-z)
    64→  - Numbers (0-9)
    65→  - Hyphens (-)
    66→- AND all other characters MUST be removed
    67→- Example: "Hello, World!" → "hello-world" (comma and exclamation removed)
    68→- Example: "Foo@Bar#123" → "foobar123" (@ and # removed)
    69→
    70→**Rationale**: Restricting to alphanumeric characters and hyphens ensures the slug is safe for URLs, file systems, and database identifiers without special encoding.
    71→
    72→---
    73→
    74→### REQ-004: Hyphen Consolidation
    75→**Priority**: Must Have
    76→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    77→**User Story**: As a developer, I want consecutive hyphens collapsed to a single hyphen so that slugs are clean and readable.
    78→
    79→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    80→- GIVEN text that would produce multiple consecutive hyphens after character removal and replacement
    81→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    82→- THEN all sequences of 2 or more consecutive hyphens MUST be replaced with a single hyphen
    83→- Example: "a---b" → "a-b"
    84→- Example: "Foo  Bar" → "foo-bar" (two spaces become one hyphen)
    85→- Example: "Hello,,,World" → "helloworld" (commas removed, no extra hyphens)
    86→
    87→**Rationale**: Multiple consecutive hyphens reduce readability and appear unprofessional in URLs.
    88→
    89→---
    90→
    91→### REQ-005: Leading and Trailing Hyphen Removal
    92→**Priority**: Must Have
    93→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
    94→**User Story**: As a developer, I want leading and trailing hyphens removed so that slugs start and end with meaningful content.
    95→
    96→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    97→- GIVEN text that would produce hyphens at the beginning or end after processing
    98→- WHEN the slugify function is called
    99→- THEN all leading hyphens MUST be removed
   100→- AND all trailing hyphens MUST be removed
   101→- Example: "  Foo  " → "foo" (not "-foo-")
   102→- Example: "---bar---" → "bar"
   103→- Example: "!!!Hello" → "hello" (exclamations removed, no leading hyphen)
   104→
   105→**Rationale**: Slugs beginning or ending with hyphens look incomplete and may cause issues with URL parsing or routing logic.
   106→
   107→---
   108→
   109→### REQ-006: Function Interface and Behavior
   110→**Priority**: Must Have
   111→**Actor**: Developer using the utility module
   112→**User Story**: As a developer, I want a simple function signature that accepts a string and returns a slug so that it is easy to use and integrate.
   113→
   114→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   115→- GIVEN the slugify function is available in the utils module
   116→- WHEN called with a single string parameter
   117→- THEN it MUST return a string representing the processed slug
   118→- AND the function MUST handle empty strings gracefully (return empty string)
   119→- AND the function MUST handle strings that become empty after processing (return empty string)
   120→- Example: slugify("") → ""
   121→- Example: slugify("!!!") → "" (all characters removed)
   122→
   123→**Rationale**: A simple, predictable interface with clear input/output behavior ensures ease of use and reduces integration errors.

   130→**Priority**: Must Have
   131→**As a**: Content creator
   132→**I want**: My article titles automatically converted to URL-safe slugs
   133→**So that**: URLs are clean, readable, and SEO-friendly

   135→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   136→- GIVEN a user enters "Hello, World!" as an article title
   137→- WHEN the system generates a slug
   138→- THEN the slug MUST be "hello-world"
   139→- AND the URL becomes "/articles/hello-world"
   140→
   141→---
   142→
   143→### STORY-002: Handle Complex Punctuation and Spacing
   144→**Priority**: Must Have
   145→**As a**: System administrator
   146→**I want**: Arbitrary text with special characters converted safely
   147→**So that**: Generated slugs never break URL routing or file naming

   152→- THEN the output MUST be "foo-bar-baz"

   158→### STORY-003: Prevent Empty or Invalid Slugs
   159→**Priority**: Should Have
